solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: American who wrote essay in verse

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe, the American writer of tales and poems
to essay is to attempt, or try

explanation.surface: An American author who produced an essay written in rhyme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'American who wrote' reads as the start of a description, but it is just the clue for Poe.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: verse is writing in metre, the general art of poems.

clue.text: They may be left out of congenial society

indicators.note: the letter for left is put out of the word for congenial

parts.note: congenial means agreeable or pleasant

explanation.surface: These people may be excluded from polite company.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also reads as a description: country folk historically shut out of genteel society.
explanation.definitionFit: Pronoun reference: the clue's subject, the country labourers, stand for the whole clue's people.

clue.text: Life model entices ex

indicators.note: to model is to shape, so these letters are moulded into a new form

explanation.surface: A tale of a model luring back a former partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'model' looks like a noun, the subject of the sentence, but works as a verb meaning shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: being alive, or being at all, is the state of being.

clue.text: Memory burdened by amnesia's beginning to wander

indicators.note: the memory carries the letter within it

parts.note: ROM is read-only memory in computing

indicators.note: takes the first letter of amnesia's

explanation.surface: Memory loss starting to make someone drift aimlessly.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to roam is to travel about with no fixed course.

clue.text: Popular writer in verse is moving

parts.note: popular things are 'in'
Andrew Motion, the English poet and former Poet Laureate

explanation.surface: A popular poet's work is emotionally stirring.
explanation.walkthrough: Andrew Motion was the UK's Poet Laureate from 1999 to 2009.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: something under way and travelling is said to be on the move, or moving.

clue.text: Going on and on endlessly about mean individual

indicators.note: turns the shortened word round to read backwards
without an end, so the word for going on and on loses its final letter

parts.note: a speech that is going on and on is dragging

explanation.surface: Someone droning on without end about a stingy person.
explanation.walkthrough: DRAGGING loses its last letter to give DRAGGIN, and 'about' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a miser or stingy person is a skinflint.

clue.text: Expert on Britain involved in drug scandal

indicators.note: the expert and Britain are wrapped up inside the drug

parts.note: opium is a narcotic drug
a pro is an expert

explanation.surface: A British specialist caught up in a narcotics scandal.
explanation.definitionFit: Related sense: public disgrace and shame are what a scandal brings.

clue.text: Fool with no time to get married in characteristic style

indicators.note: says the time letter is removed from the fool

parts.note: an idiot is a fool

explanation.surface: A fool in a hurry to wed, in typical fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a manner of expression peculiar to an artist or language is its mode or style.

clue.text: Swift upset leaders of Enlightenment by mercilessly lampooning new ideas

indicators.note: the collected letters are knocked over into a new order
takes the first letter of each of the following six words

explanation.surface: Jonathan Swift annoyed Enlightenment thinkers by savagely mocking fresh ideas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swift' looks like Jonathan Swift, the satirist, but is the definition meaning quick.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: quick and agile movement is fast and light on the feet.

clue.text: Several engagements may result in this large armed force eliminating resistance

definitions.text: Several engagements may result in this

parts.note: large means big

indicators.note: the armed force drops the letter for resistance

parts.note: an army is an armed force
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A huge army, having crushed the resistance, after several military engagements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engagements' suggests battles, but here means promises to marry.
explanation.definitionFit: Legal consequence: marrying more than once while still wed is the crime of having multiple spouses.

clue.text: Disturbing process over time inspires French director

indicators.note: to inspire is literally to breathe in, so the process takes the director inside it

parts.note: growing older, the process time works on everyone, is aging
Jacques Tati, the French film director of Monsieur Hulot fame

explanation.surface: An unsettling slow process gives a French filmmaker his inspiration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inspires' reads as encouraging the director, but literally means breathing him in. Jacques Tati made the Monsieur Hulot comedies.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: disturbing and stirring things up both describe causing unrest or upset.

clue.text: Shape the doctrine of public relations?

parts.note: an ism is any doctrine or creed

explanation.surface: A question asking how to give public relations a guiding doctrine.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces come in the reverse of the clue's order: PR first, then ISM.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a prism is a solid geometric figure, one kind of shape.

clue.text: Key character that's central to authorial voice

parts.note: Alt is a key on a computer keyboard

indicators.note: a character is a letter, and the one central to authorial is its middle letter; that the answer also runs through 'central to' is a coincidence

explanation.surface: A crucial letter sitting at the core of an author's distinctive voice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key character' reads as one phrase but splits: 'Key' gives ALT and 'character' starts the middle-letter pick, the O of authorial.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: alto is a singing voice, the range below soprano.

clue.text: Irrational double standard reinforcing a vacuous appeal

indicators.note: the two standards give support on either side of the a, holding it between them

parts.note: two words for a standard: par and norm

indicators.note: empty, so only the outside letters of appeal are kept

explanation.surface: A hypocritical rule bolstering a hollow plea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'double standard' reads as hypocrisy but means two words for a standard; 'reinforcing' has them flank the A, and the emptied appeal follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose synonym: phenomena beyond scientific explanation defy reason, so they can be called irrational.

clue.text: Pleads with top players for audience south of Bury

indicators.note: in a down clue the second piece sits below the first

parts.note: to inter is to bury

indicators.note: the word is as heard by listeners

parts.note: seeds are the top-ranked players in a tournament

explanation.surface: Someone appealing to the best performers for a hearing, south of the town of Bury.
explanation.walkthrough: Bury, capitalised, looks like the Lancashire town but is the verb. Seeds sound like CEDES.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to intervene on another's behalf is to make an appeal for them.

clue.text: Property right in the heart of westerly French city

indicators.note: takes the two middle letters of westerly

parts.note: Nancy is a city in north-eastern France

explanation.surface: A legal entitlement to property located in the middle of a western French city.
explanation.definitionFit: Legal sense: holding land or a building as a tenant is a right to occupy property.

clue.text: Relating to the back part of pilchard or salmon

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Talk of the rear section of two oily fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part of' looks like part of the definition ('the back part'), but it signals the hidden word.
explanation.definitionFit: Anatomical term: a fish's dorsal fin sits on its back, the upper side.

clue.text: Effect of numbers entering system unsettled most of East Anglia

indicators.note: disturbed, so the letters are rearranged
drops the last letter of East

explanation.surface: The impact of figures pouring into an unstable network across eastern England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'numbers' here means things that numb, painkillers, not figures. East Anglia is the region of eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Medical sense: painkillers absorbed into the body bring loss of pain sensation.

clue.text: The result of transitioning if gender is manipulated digitally

indicators.note: transitioning means changing, so the letters change into a new order

explanation.surface: What happens when gender identity is altered electronically.
explanation.walkthrough: 'digitally' suggests computers, but means with the fingers.
explanation.definitionFit: Literal sense: something handled with the fingers has been touched or felt by hand.

clue.text: Timeless secrets could be hidden here

definitions.text: Timeless secrets could be hidden here

indicators.note: says the letters may become something else, a rearrangement
means without, so one letter is dropped from secrets

explanation.surface: An alcove where age-old secrets might be stashed away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Timeless' splits into 'Time' (T) and 'less': SECRETS without T leaves SERCES, which rearranges to the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: an alcove or hidden nook set into a wall is just the place to stash things.

clue.text: Produce a mark for each go in some haste

parts.note: a scar is a mark left on the skin
per means for each

explanation.surface: Making a mark on every attempt in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: To scarper is British slang for running off quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang synonym: running away fast is bolting or fleeing.

clue.text: Yorkshire newspaper writer's article about cause of flooding

parts.note: Yorkshire dialect shortens 'the' to t', so the Sun newspaper is T'Sun

indicators.note: turns the writer's I'M plus A round to read backwards

parts.note: the writer is 'I', so writer's is I'm (I am)
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A northern columnist's piece on why towns flood.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun is a British tabloid; in Yorkshire 'the' is famously clipped to t'. 'about' turns I'M A round into AMI.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a giant sea wave raised by an undersea earthquake swamps coastlines.

clue.text: Admit (after a bit of thought) it get's on one's wick

indicators.note: places the word for admit after that letter
takes the first letter of thought

parts.note: to admit is to allow

explanation.surface: Confessing, after some reflection, that something really irritates you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets on one's wick' is British slang for annoys; literally, candle fat coats the wick. The apostrophe in get's is a slip the setter acknowledged.
explanation.definitionFit: Literal reading: animal fat used for candles clings to and burns on the candle's wick.

clue.text: Rising anger topped scale of potential differences

indicators.note: the first letter of the word for anger is cut off

parts.note: ire is anger
the volt is the unit for measuring electrical potential difference

explanation.surface: Mounting fury exceeded the range of possible disagreements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' looks like an adjective for the anger but is the definition, a noun for an uprising.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an uprising against authority is a rebellion.

clue.text: Particularly unusual places I see houses

indicators.note: the cathedral city holds the rearranged letters inside it

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city, and a bishop's see

indicators.note: says the letters of places and I are arranged in an odd way

explanation.surface: Someone noticing that they find strange places in particular.
explanation.walkthrough: 'see' looks like a verb but is a bishop's diocese; Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, and 'houses' puts the rearranged letters inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: both adverbs mean above all or more than usual.

clue.text: Writer suppressing case for climate change

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument; suppressing, pressing down from above, sets it on top of the next piece in this down clue

indicators.note: takes the outside letters of climate

explanation.surface: An author stifling the argument for climate change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suppressing' just places the pen above the next piece in this down clue. 'climate change' reads as one phrase, but 'change' is the definition: loose coins.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: small coins in the pocket are loose cash.

clue.text: Keen to know more about fellows shrouded in cigarette smoke

indicators.note: the fellows wrap around what is left, so lifting them out of the smoke reveals it

parts.note: fag fog: fag is British slang for a cigarette, and fog is smoke
F is the abbreviation for fellow, so two of them are FF

explanation.surface: Curious about men lost in a haze of tobacco smoke.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer, with two F's about it (F-A-G-F-O-G), is shrouded in FAG FOG; take the fellows out to leave it. 'Fag' is British slang for a cigarette.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: being eagerly curious and excited about news is the sense of wide-eyed anticipation.

clue.text: Part of course that's not supported by bar

indicators.note: says the piece is taken away from the word

parts.note: a lesson is one part of a course of study
a thing that sits on something is supported by it

explanation.surface: A section of a course that the bar won't support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' looks like a pub or a rail but is the preposition meaning except.
explanation.definitionFit: Preposition synonym: 'bar one' means except one, minus one.

clue.text: Wife beset by heartless and capricious demon is possessed

indicators.note: the wife is surrounded by the rearranged letters
unpredictable, so the letters are shuffled
drops the middle letter of demon

explanation.surface: A woman tormented by a fickle demon is possessed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' takes the M out of DEMON, leaving DEON; 'capricious' rearranges that to ONED, which surrounds W.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something held as one's property is had or belonging to someone.

clue.text: One who claims poor serfs must be radicalised

indicators.note: radicalising changes things at the root, so the letters are turned into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone asserting that impoverished peasants have to be stirred into revolt.
explanation.walkthrough: One who professes something is one who claims it.
explanation.definitionFit: Literal sense: someone who professes a belief or ability declares it openly.

clue.text: Tramp trades daughter for guaranteed value

indicators.note: swaps one letter out of the word for a new piece in its place

parts.note: to tramp is to tread heavily
a guaranteed thing is sure

explanation.surface: A vagrant gives up his daughter in exchange for something of certain worth.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb synonym: to prize or cherish something is to hold it dear.

clue.text: Diesel banned at regular intervals in Greenland?

indicators.note: takes every second letter of Diesel banned

explanation.surface: A ban on diesel cars at set times in Greenland.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks Greenland as an example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Greenland is the largest body of land surrounded by sea on Earth.
